root_cause.text: In `virtio_net`’s RSS header management (`virtnet_set_queues()`), a `devm_kzalloc()` allocation made against `virtio_device->dev` was later released with `devm_kfree()` using `net_device->dev`, so the managed resource was tracked against the wrong device object and triggered a devres mismatch warning.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes all RSS header allocation/free calls from `&dev->dev` to `&vi->vdev->dev`, and the commit message explicitly says “Initial rss_hdr allocation uses virtio_device->device, but virtnet_set_queues() frees using net_device->device,” identifying the device mismatch as the bug cause.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes all RSS header allocation/free calls from `&dev->dev` to `&vi->vdev->dev`, and the commit message explicitly says “Initial rss_hdr allocation uses virtio_device->device, but virtnet_set_queues() frees using net_device->device,” identifying the device mismatch as the bug cause.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the virtio device as the devm allocation owner for RSS header memory in virtnet_set_queues().
intent_record.what: In virtnet_set_queues(), the devm_kzalloc() call that allocates vi->rss_hdr was changed to use &vi->vdev->dev instead of &dev->dev as the device argument.
intent_record.how: This makes the RSS header allocation managed by the virtio device's lifetime rather than the net_device's embedded device object, ensuring the allocation is tied to the correct device context while preserving the existing error handling and fallback to the old RSS header on allocation failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the RSS rollback cleanup to free vi->rss_hdr with the correct virtio device context after a failed RSS command commit.
intent_record.what: In the error path of virtnet_set_queues(), the call to devm_kfree() was changed to free vi->rss_hdr using &vi->vdev->dev instead of &dev->dev.
intent_record.how: This makes the RSS header memory be released against the virtio device's dev pointer rather than an unrelated or incorrect dev reference, ensuring the cleanup path uses the proper device context when RSS command commitment fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the device used when freeing old_rss_hdr so the managed allocation is released against the correct virtio device.
intent_record.what: In virtnet_set_queues(), the devm_kfree() call for old_rss_hdr was changed to free memory using &vi->vdev->dev instead of &dev->dev.
intent_record.how: This changes the device context associated with the managed free operation, ensuring the allocation is released against the same virtio device object that likely owns it, which avoids mismatched device-managed memory handling.

Fix the RSS rollback cleanup to free vi->rss_hdr with the correct virtio device context after a failed RSS command commit.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix the device ownership used for managed RSS header memory allocation/freeing in virtnet_set_queues() so it is tied to the correct virtio device.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the reported devres mismatch in virtio_net RSS header management by using the virtio device for both devm allocation and freeing of old_rss_hdr in virtnet_set_queues(), which matches the root cause.
The change directly matches the root cause: it corrects RSS header cleanup to use the proper virtio device context, fixing the devm allocation/free device mismatch in virtio_net RSS management.

candidates.rationale: This is the managed allocation site for the RSS header memory. The root cause is that the allocation was tied to the wrong device object, which later caused devres tracking mismatch when the memory was freed.

This is the corresponding free site using the same incorrect device context. The mismatch between the allocation/free ownership and the intended virtio device is the direct source of the devres warning.
This cleanup path frees the allocated RSS header with the wrong device context after a failed RSS command commit, which is part of the ownership mismatch described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation stores the RSS header as a devres resource owned by the wrong device object. The vulnerability root cause is the devm ownership mismatch in virtnet_set_queues(), where the resource was later managed/freed under a different device context, triggering the devres warning.

This free uses the same incorrect device context as the allocation, reinforcing the devres tracking mismatch. The root cause describes that RSS header memory was allocated against one device but released through another, which leads to the managed-resource mismatch warning.

This rollback cleanup path frees the RSS header with the wrong device owner after a failed commit. It is part of the same ownership mismatch in virtnet_set_queues() that caused the devres mismatch warning.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 4944be2f5ad8c74b93e4e272f3a0f1a136bbc438
Author: Akihiko Odaki <akihiko.odaki@daynix.com>

    virtio_net: Allocate rss_hdr with devres
    
    virtnet_probe() lacks the code to free rss_hdr in its error path.
    Allocate rss_hdr with devres so that it will be automatically freed.
    
    Fixes: 86a48a00efdf ("virtio_net: Support dynamic rss indirection table size")
    Signed-off-by: Akihiko Odaki <akihiko.odaki@daynix.com>
    Acked-by: Jason Wa
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this commit version. The diff changes allocation and free to use the same device object consistently: `vi->rss_hdr = devm_kzalloc(&dev->dev, ...)` in `virtnet_set_queues()` and `vi->rss_hdr = devm_kzalloc(&vdev->dev, ...)` in `virtnet_probe()`, with matching `devm_kfree(&dev->dev, ...)` for the queue-management path. There is no longer a `devm_kfree()` using `net_device->dev` for memory allocated against `virtio_device->dev`, so the devres mismatch warning root cause is fixed here. The removal path also drops the old manual `kfree(vi->rss_hdr);`, consistent with devres-managed ownership.
